compiled_rows: This golden-furred cat loves to eat, and mice
are its favorite.
Squeeze this magic lime as often as you like.
It always yields juice to quench the crew's
thirst at sea.
This mystic ring holds the soul of Hermes,
travel god and one of the twelve Olympians.
It's said to protect sailors in storms.
The recipe comes from Hua Tuo, a famed
physician of China's Three Kingdoms era. They
say a tiny dose cures any contagious disease.
A slender sword with a blade and hilt painted
glossy black.
A broadsword supposedly used by Laocoon, priest
of ancient Troy.
The legendary knight Lohengrin is said to have
carried this saber. Its blade is longer and
sharper than most.
Its S-shaped blade gleams like a golden
crescent moon.
An ornate curved sword regarded
as the mark of a hero.
A very heavy military sword made
entirely of gold.
Plain and practical, this sword is easy
to wield and mysteriously fills its holder
with courage.
An Indian saber with countless lapis beads,
said to be ancient.
At first glance, it's just an old sword.
An admiral who swept pirates from nearby waters
is said to have prized it.
A broad crescent blade. A fleet deputy is
said to have struck down a sailor on the spot
for urging betrayal of the admiral.
A dagger with an H-shaped hilt, strange colors
and unusual ornaments. Its origins are unknown.
A two-handed blade that glows white
for no known reason.
This crescent blade has a red tint that brings
to mind all the blood it has spilled.
Known as the Betrayer's Sword, it has an eerie
air, as though an evil spirit possessed it.
Zhao Yun, a famed Shu general
of the Three Kingdoms era, is said to have used
this spear. He was best with a spear.
An error in a general's plans cost
a close ally's life. He gave this superb sword
to the family as an apology.
A red-haired woman pirate famed for her beauty
used this sword. It's prized as a treasure and
for its keen edge.
The mythical bull-headed Minotaur supposedly
wielded this huge, mighty axe.
This strange cooking knife becomes a powerful
weapon in the hands of someone who's angry.
A vivid sky-blue knife said to grant
Aztec water god Tlaloc's protection.
A fine yet eerie axe with a black handle and
twisted tip.
The Mongol hero Kublai Khan wielded
this superb greatsword. It strikes
with tremendous force from above.
A legendary spear with a fiery gleam. Ares,
god of war and one of the twelve Olympians, is
said to have wielded it.
This holy sword is said to have been carried by
Britain's legendary King Arthur. Its blade is
strong enough to split rock.
This Japanese sword has an eerie aura and
an edge second to none. Legend says something
will befall its owner.

2836: Squeeze this magic lime as often as you like. It always yields juice to quench the crew’s thirst at sea.
Use two natural sentences and keep both the inexhaustible juice and its benefit at sea.
2837: This mystic ring holds the soul of Hermes, travel god and one of the twelve Olympians. It’s said to protect sailors in storms.
Preserve the mystery of the ring, Hermes’s place among the Twelve and his protection against storms.
2838: The recipe comes from Hua Tuo, a famed physician of China’s Three Kingdoms era. They say a tiny dose cures any contagious disease.
Attribute the remedy’s recipe to the renowned physician and the efficacy claim to the game’s tradition. Keep the small dose together.
2842: Its S-shaped blade gleams like a golden crescent moon.
Keep the shape, golden gleam and moon image together.
2843: An ornate curved sword regarded as the mark of a hero.
Keep the traditional association with heroism and leave how the sword is displayed unstated.
2847: At first glance, it’s just an old sword. An admiral who swept pirates from nearby waters is said to have prized it.
Restore the plain first impression and the admiral’s attachment to the blade.
2848: A broad crescent blade. A fleet deputy is said to have struck down a sailor on the spot for urging betrayal of the admiral.
Preserve the fleet deputy and leave the target of the sailor’s urging unspecified.
2851: This crescent blade has a red tint that brings to mind all the blood it has spilled.
Keep the image of past bloodshed tied to the blade’s color.
2853: Zhao Yun, a famed Shu general of the Three Kingdoms era, is said to have used this spear. He was best with a spear.
Restore Zhao Yun’s role and preserve the traditional attribution.
2854: An error in a general’s plans cost a close ally’s life. He gave this superb sword to the family as an apology.
Keep the general’s responsibility, the gift to the family and its purpose clear.
2855: A red-haired woman pirate famed for her beauty used this sword. It’s prized as a treasure and for its keen edge.
Restore the pirate’s identity and keep both the blade’s keen edge and value as a treasure.
2860: The Mongol hero Kublai Khan wielded this superb greatsword. It strikes with tremendous force from above.
Keep the named owner and both observations about the sword.
